title: BroxGeneralNormConstrainedPL.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective may be nonconvex. It is bounded below on a nonempty closed convex feasible set C, differentiable at every point of C, and satisfies ‖Df(y)−Df(x)‖_* ≤ L‖y−x‖ for x,y ∈ C.

problem_class.label: pl
problem_class.details: For every x ∈ C, 2μ(f(x)−inf_C f) ≤ (inf_{n ∈ N_C(x)} ‖Df(x)+n‖_*)², where N_C(x) consists of the dual functionals n satisfying n(z−x) ≤ 0 for all z ∈ C.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: At any feasible query x, oracle 0 returns the exact Fréchet derivative Df(x) as a continuous linear functional for every history and seed.

oracle.label: linear_minimization
oracle.details: Given x ∈ C, any radius ρ ≥ 0, and any dual functional g, oracle 1 returns an exact minimizer of g over C ∩ {z : ‖z−x‖ ≤ ρ}. Ties may be resolved using the history and seed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: The norm on E is arbitrary. It defines the local oracle balls, and its dual norm measures both gradient variation and the normal-cone residual.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real normed space of arbitrary dimension.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The algorithm receives E, L > 0, r > 0, and the feasible starting point x₀. The PL modulus μ > 0, initial gap bound Δ ≥ f(x₀)−inf_C f, and target ε > 0 enter the oracle budgets but are hidden from the algorithm.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BroxGeneralNormConstrainedPL.lean, Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible. LongTails/Template.lean, Convergence.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point x must satisfy f(x)−inf_C f ≤ ε.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The same returned point must belong to C.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the objective-gap bound must hold jointly with probability one under the product of the algorithm and oracle seed laws at the prescribed per-oracle budgets.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines a constrained PL inequality on the dual normal-cone residual with exact linear minimization over variable-radius feasible balls in an arbitrary norm. Gradient calls and local minimization calls have separate budgets, and the algorithm receives neither the PL modulus nor the initial gap bound.

descriptionHtml:
Constrained Polyak–Łojasiewicz Minimization

We consider minimizing a possibly nonconvex function f:E→R over a closed convex set C in a finite-dimensional real normed space E. On C, the objective is bounded below, has a Lipschitz derivative, and satisfies a constrained Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality. A given feasible point has bounded initial objective gap. At feasible points, one oracle returns the exact derivative and another returns a minimizer of a supplied linear functional over the intersection of C with a query ball centered at the point. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈C satisfying f(x¯)−infz∈Cf(z)≤ε almost surely.

Write f⋆ for the value of the problem infx∈Cf(x). The algorithm receives only E, the smoothness constant L>0, a radius parameter r>0, and the starting point x0. The Polyak–Łojasiewicz constant μ>0, the initial gap bound Δ∈R, and ε may enter the oracle-call budgets. Write E∗ for the continuous dual of E and ∥⋅∥op for its induced operator norm.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Feasibility and initial gap). The set C is closed and convex, x0∈C, and f⋆>−∞,f(x0)−f⋆≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Smoothness on the feasible set). The function f is Fréchet differentiable at every x∈C. Its derivative Df(x)∈E∗ satisfies ∥Df(y)−Df(x)∥op≤L∥y−x∥,x,y∈C.

Assumption 3 (Constrained Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality). For x∈C, define the normal cone and stationarity residual by NC(x)={n∈E∗:n(z−x)≤0 for all z∈C},sC(x)=infn∈NC(x)∥Df(x)+n∥op. The objective satisfies μ(f(x)−f⋆)≤12sC(x)2,x∈C.

Derivative calls and local linear minimization calls are counted separately. The derivative oracle returns Df(x) at x∈C. A local linear minimization query specifies a center x∈C, any radius ρ≥0, and a functional g∈E∗. The oracle returns a point v∈argminz∈C, ∥z−x∥≤ρg(z). After the allotted calls, the output must satisfy x¯∈Candf(x¯)−f⋆≤εP-a.s., where P is the joint law of the independent algorithm and oracle randomness.

theorems.referencesHtml: • Peter Richtárik and Xun Qian. Broximal Gradient Descent in General Norms: Convergence without Fejér Monotonicity. 2026 (arXiv v1). Complexity: warm-started radius halving reaches objective gap ε in O(K) exact gradient calls and O(K+log4+⁡(r2(8L2/μ+6L)/ε)) local linear minimization calls, including rejected trials. For initial gap Δ0=f(x0)−infCf>ε>0, K=⌊log4⁡(1+6Δ0/(Lr2))⌋+⌈log⁡(Δ0/ε)/log⁡(1+μ/(25L))⌉, and log4+⁡(t)=max{0,log4⁡t}. If Δ0≤ε, the initial point already meets the target.
theorems.formulaHtml: Oracle 0:KwhereK=⌊log4⁡(1+6⋅ΔL⋅r2)⌋++⌈log1+μ25⋅L⁡(Δε)⌉+ Oracle 1:2⋅K+⌈log4⁡(r2⋅(8⋅L2μ+6⋅L)ε)⌉+whereK=⌊log4⁡(1+6⋅ΔL⋅r2)⌋++⌈log1+μ25⋅L⁡(Δε)⌉+

comparisonHtml:
In a finite-dimensional real normed space, C is closed and convex and x0∈C. The objective is bounded below on C and differentiable at each point of C, with L-Lipschitz derivative in the dual norm. On C, μ(f(x)−f⋆)≤s(x)2/2. The oracles give exact gradients and exact local LMOs with arbitrary tie-breaking. For L,μ,r,ε>0, the target, guaranteed almost surely, is x∈C with f(x)−f⋆≤ε.

Sufficient budgets for general-norm constrained PL minimization.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) WarmHalvingBroxGeneralNorm (Ours) (review) O(1+H(Δ)+log+⁡(Δ/ε)log⁡(1+μ/L))
(2) (Richtárik and Qian 2026), Thm. 30 and Cor. 31 O(1+H(Δ0)+log⁡(Δ0/ε)log⁡(1+μ/L)) (1): Matches the known rate in Lean for 0<ε<Δ0. Requires differentiability only at points of C, covers all ε>0, and certifies the fixed-budget output. (1): One extra local-LMO call in the allowance, plus rounding.
(3) (Garber and Hazan 2015), Alg. 2, Lemmas 1–2, exact local oracle O(1+Lμlog+⁡(D/ε)) (1): Extends the Euclidean strongly convex polytope guarantee with vertex start to normal-cone PL without attainment. The strongly convex rate transfers to general norms. With Δ=D and μ≤L, matches the leading order without knowing μ,D. (1): On the overlap, needs r, adds H(Δ), and has a larger leading constant in the logarithmic accuracy term.
(4) (Richtárik et al. 2026), Thm. 3.3 O(1+Lμlog⁡(D/ε)) (1): Extends Euclidean strong convexity with neighborhood differentiability, attainment and 0<μ≤L to general-norm PL. For 0<ε<D, matches the leading rate on the overlap with Δ=D, without knowing μ,D. (1): Needs r and adds H(Δ) on the overlap. No squared-distance guarantee.
(5) (Richtárik et al. 2026), Thm. 3.6, strongly convex case O(1+log+⁡(Δ0/ε)log⁡(1+ξ2μ/L)) accepted steps. No total-call bound. (1): Counts all trials on the globally smooth Euclidean strongly convex overlap with attainment. Extends to general norms and normal-cone PL with smoothness on C. (1): Needs r on the overlap.
(6) (Richtárik et al. 2026), Thm. D.16, γ=1/L O(1+log+⁡(Δ0/ε)−log⁡(1−μ/L)), with one gradient, local LMO and projection per step. (1): General norms and normal-cone PL extend Euclidean projected-gradient PL with attainment and neighborhood smoothness. On the overlap, removes projections. (1): Needs r on the overlap.

Abbr: f⋆=infCf, Δ0=f(x0)−f⋆, and Δ,D≥Δ0 are gap bounds (D>0 is supplied to the method). s(x)=infn∈NC(x)∥∇f(x)+n∥∗, with NC(x) the normal cone. A local LMO minimizes a linear form on C intersected with the closed query ball. Costs sum gradient and local-LMO calls unless indicated. r is the initial radius cap, ξ∈(0,1) the backtracking factor, and log+⁡t=max{0,log⁡t} with log+⁡0=0. H(a)=log⁡(1+a/(Lr2))+log+⁡(r2L(1+L/μ)/ε). In (3)–(5), μ is the strong-convexity modulus. In (6), μ is the projected PL modulus, with 0<μ≤L for a positive initial gap. The quotient is zero at μ=L.

Garber, Dan, and Elad Hazan. 2015. A Linearly Convergent Conditional Gradient Algorithm with Applications to Online and Stochastic Optimization. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1301.4666.
Richtárik, Peter, Kaja Gruntkowska, and Hanmin Li. 2026. Broximal Gradient Descent: A Projection-Free Sister of Projected Gradient Descent. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2605.08850.
Richtárik, Peter, and Xun Qian. 2026. Broximal Gradient Descent in General Norms: Convergence Without Fejér Monotonicity. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2611.24645.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

open Set MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.BroxGeneralNormConstrainedPL

open OracleTemplate

abbrev BroxQuery (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] :=
  E ⊕ (E × ℝ × (E →L[ℝ] ℝ))

abbrev BroxReply (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] :=
  (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) ⊕ E

def normalCone {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (C : Set E) (x : E) :
    Set (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) :=
  {n | ∀ z ∈ C, n (z - x) ≤ 0}

noncomputable def stationarity {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (f : E → ℝ) (C : Set E) (x : E) : ℝ :=
  sInf ((fun n => ‖fderiv ℝ f x + n‖) '' normalCone C x)

noncomputable def optimalValue {E : Type*} (f : E → ℝ) (C : Set E) : ℝ :=
  sInf (f '' C)

structure Public where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [spaceE : NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  L : ℝ
  r : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.spaceE Public.finiteE

structure Params extends Public where
  μ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  f : p.E → ℝ
  C : Set p.E

abbrev spec : Setup where
  numOracles := 2
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := BroxQuery p.E
  Reply p := BroxReply p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p.toPublic
  valid p := 0 < p.L ∧ 0 < p.μ ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧ 0 < p.r
  admissible p I O :=
    Convex ℝ I.C ∧ IsClosed I.C ∧ p.x0 ∈ I.C ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.C, DifferentiableAt ℝ I.f x) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.C, ∀ y ∈ I.C, ‖fderiv ℝ I.f y - fderiv ℝ I.f x‖ ≤ p.L * ‖y - x‖) ∧
    BddBelow (I.f '' I.C) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.C, p.μ * (I.f x - optimalValue I.f I.C) ≤ stationarity I.f I.C x ^ 2 / 2) ∧
    I.f p.x0 - optimalValue I.f I.C ≤ p.Δ ∧
    (∀ history seed x, x ∈ I.C →
      O.answer history (0, .inl x) seed = .inl (fderiv ℝ I.f x)) ∧
    (∀ history seed x r g, x ∈ I.C → 0 ≤ r →
      ∃ v ∈ I.C, ‖v - x‖ ≤ r ∧ (∀ z ∈ I.C, ‖z - x‖ ≤ r → g v ≤ g z) ∧
        O.answer history (1, .inr (x, r, g)) seed = .inr v)
  successful p I output P :=
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), output ω ∈ I.C ∧ I.f (output ω) - optimalValue I.f I.C ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.BroxGeneralNormConstrainedPL
